cards.explanation: The answer is old and gray, friends. Samuel says, "…I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you." He's standing there with the new king in front of everybody and saying it plain. He adds that he has walked before them from his youth until this day. That's a whole lifetime of showing up.

The answer is to give it back to them, friends. Samuel asks, "Whose ox or donkey have I taken?" and so on, then says, "Tell me, and I will restore it to you." He's ready to pay it all back. A man who offers that is either very clean or very brave, and I think it's both.

The answer is False, friends. The people reply, "You have not cheated us or oppressed us…" and say he has not taken anything from the hand of man. Samuel then says the LORD and His anointed are witnesses that they have found nothing in his hand, and the people answer, "He is a witness…"
The answer is Aaron, friends. Samuel says the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought the fathers out of Egypt (1 Samuel 12:8). Aaron was Moses' partner in the job. Two leaders, one rescue.
The answer is True, friends. Samuel says, "But they forgot the LORD their God…" They were brought out and settled in the land, and then they forgot Him. I think that's a hard turn.

The answer is that they had forsaken the LORD, friends. They cried out, "We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and Ashtoreths." They owned it right there in the middle of the trouble. Then they asked to be delivered so they could serve Him.

The answer is True, friends. Samuel says, "So the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Barak, Jephthah, and Samuel…" Samuel is the last name on the list. He just slips himself in at the end and keeps walking, and I'd have needed a drumroll.

The word is securely, friends. Samuel says the LORD delivered them from the hands of their enemies on every side, "…and you dwelt securely." Enemies on every side, and then safe. That's a good day's work, and it was the LORD's.
The answer is the LORD their God, friends. Samuel says they asked for a king "…even though the LORD your God was your king." They already had the best King there is.

The answer is True, friends. Samuel says if they fear the LORD, serve Him and obey His voice, and if both they and their king follow the LORD their God, "…then all will be well." Notice the king is in that "if" too. Everybody follows, everybody's fine.

The word is against, friends. Samuel says, "…then the hand of the LORD will be against you as it was against your fathers." It's a serious warning, and he says it plainly. The fathers' story he just told is the example.

The answer is thunder and rain, friends. Samuel says, "I will call on the LORD to send thunder and rain…" And he points out it's the wheat harvest. Thunder and rain at harvest time is not what anybody orders.

The answer is the evil of asking for a king, friends. Samuel says it's so "…that you will know and see what a great evil you have committed in the sight of the LORD by asking for a king." The thunder and rain are the sign for it. It's a heavy word, so I'll leave it right there.

The word is feared, friends. The text says, "…all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel." Samuel called to the LORD, and on that day the LORD sent thunder and rain. As a result, the people feared.

The answer is "Do not be afraid," friends. Samuel answers them, "Do not be afraid…" The crowd was begging not to die, and the first thing out of his mouth is comfort. Then he goes on to tell them how to keep going.

The answer is False, friends. Samuel says, "Even though you have committed all this evil, do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart." He doesn't tell them to quit. He tells them to stay and serve with everything they've got.

The answer is that He was pleased to make them His own, friends. Samuel says the LORD will not abandon His people "…because He was pleased to make you His own." It's about what He chose, not what they earned.

The word is praying, friends. Samuel says, "…far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you." He won't stop praying for them. That's a promise from a man who knows how they just acted.
The answer is False, friends. Samuel says, "But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away." Both, not only the king. It's a serious ending.
